name: multipliers-compound-multiplicatively
prompt: Estimate the upgrade effort for one of our own TYPO3 extensions going from v13 to v14.3. It uses $GLOBALS['TSFE'] in two places, ships three custom ViewHelpers with untyped arguments, and its TypoScript sets config.concatenateCss = 1. Rector is available. Show the calculation.

assertions.description: Applies the TypoScriptFrontendController-removal multiplier of 1.3
Applies the Fluid 5 strict-typing and asset-concat multipliers of 1.2
Compounds the factors multiplicatively rather than adding them
Applies the Rector auto-fix discount of 0.80-0.85 after the factor multipliers
Starts from the documented v13 to v14.3 baseline of 4-8 hours per own extension

samples.passing: Baseline for an own extension on v13 → v14.3 is 4–8 h. Three factors apply and they are multiplicative: TSFE removal × 1.3, Fluid 5 strict VH typing × 1.2, asset-concat removal × 1.2, so the product is 1.87. Then apply the Rector discount × 0.80–0.85. That gives roughly 6–13 h before your team calibration factor.
failing: Add the factors up: 1.3 + 1.2 + 1.2 means about 3.7 times the baseline, so 15–30 hours.
Roughly two days per extension. TYPO3 upgrades are hard to quantify, so add a generous buffer and re-estimate later.

name: calibration-is-not-a-multiplier
prompt: Your model gives 4-8 hours per own extension for v13 to v14.3. Our team is consistently faster than that. Do we add a 0.7 factor to the risk multiplier table?

assertions.description: Names team speed as calibration rather than a risk factor
Keeps calibration out of the multiplier table, in a team-specific overlay
Explains the split: factors are objective trigger conditions, calibration is team-specific (typically 0.6-1.4)

samples.passing: No — keep it out of the multiplier table. A risk multiplier applies when a trigger condition matches, objectively and regardless of team. How fast your team works at the same factor count is calibration, typically 0.6–1.4, and it belongs in a thin team overlay skill that imports this model.
failing: Yes, add a 0.7 team-speed multiplier to references/risk-multipliers.md alongside the other factors.
Just lower the baselines in the table to 3–6 hours so the numbers match what you observe.

name: v14-target-is-14-3-not-14-0
prompt: We are planning a TYPO3 v14 upgrade. Which v14 version should we target, and how large is the breaking-change cycle?

assertions.description: Targets v14.3, the LTS release
Rules out 14.0-14.2 as unsupported sprint releases
Quantifies the cycle with the documented 98 breaking-change entries
Names the 31 deprecation entries alongside the breaking ones

samples.passing: Target v14.3 LTS, released 2026-04-21. Sprint releases 14.0–14.2 are unsupported. The cycle is the largest in years: 98 breaking and 31 deprecation entries, all landed in v14.0.
failing: Target 14.0 — it is the first v14 release, so you get the longest runway before 15 arrives.
Any v14 release will do; the breaking changes are spread evenly across the 14.x line.

name: rector-count-and-discount-v14
prompt: How much does typo3-rector help with a v14 migration, and how do I express that in an estimate?

assertions.description: States the 47 v14-specific Rector rules
Applies it as a 0.80-0.85 discount rather than as a percentage saved
States that the discount covers mechanical edits, not verification

name: php-first-then-typo3
prompt: We are on TYPO3 12.4 with PHP 8.1 and want to reach 13.4 with PHP 8.4. In which order should we move?

assertions.description: Raises PHP before the TYPO3 major
Names 8.4 as reachable on the current 12.4 already
Gives the reason: it isolates PHP failures from TYPO3 failures during debugging

samples.passing: Raise PHP first: 12.4 already supports 8.4, so move to 8.4 on 12.4, test there, fix the PHP-level failures (undefined array keys above all), and only then upgrade TYPO3 to 13.4. That isolates 'is this PHP or TYPO3?' while debugging instead of leaving both variables in play.
failing: Upgrade TYPO3 to 13.4 first, then raise PHP to 8.4 afterwards — 13.4 supports 8.2 so the old PHP is fine during the upgrade.
Do both in the same deployment to save a release cycle.

assertions.description: Estimates core extensions at zero hours

name: stale-third-party-options-and-range

Names forking as an option
Prefers fork plus upstream patch over maintaining a local fork forever
Names replacement as the highest-effort option that can invalidate the timeline

name: trigger-detection-is-a-grep
prompt: How do I decide which v14 risk multipliers apply to a given extension? I do not want to read every file.

assertions.description: Decides each factor by a mechanical search rather than by judgement
Names at least one concrete trigger token from the multiplier table
Frames a multiplier as applying when its trigger condition matches

name: post-upgrade-wizard-only-if-transited
prompt: Does our v13 to v14.3 estimate need extra time for the be_users credential-data upgrade wizard?

assertions.description: Identifies the change by number
Prices it at the documented +0.5-1 hour
Applies it conditionally: only if the project transited through v14.2

samples.passing: Only if the project actually transited through v14.2 — then add +0.5–1 h for the #109585 be_users credential-data wizard. A direct v13 → v14.3 path does not need it.
failing: Yes, always add a day for post-upgrade wizards; every v14 upgrade needs the #109585 wizard.
No, upgrade wizards never take measurable time and do not belong in an estimate.

name: skip-version-cumulative-not-triple
prompt: We are on TYPO3 11.5. Is it cheaper to go 11 to 12 to 13 to 14, or straight to 14.3?

assertions.description: States that all intermediate breaking changes still apply
States that the skip path is a single effort rather than the sum of three upgrades
Notes that the saving comes from testing and release cycles done once

name: conformance-score-feeds-the-estimate

assertions.description: Names the conformance skill as the quality input
Separates estimation from the skills that perform the upgrade
States that the conformance result feeds the risk multiplier rather than being a separate estimate

name: estimation-formula-order-of-operations
prompt: Write out the per-extension estimation formula this model uses.

assertions.description: Starts from the per-path baseline
Includes the Rector discount
Includes the team calibration factor as the last term
Includes the product of the applicable risk multipliers

samples.passing: extension_hours = baseline × Π(risk multipliers) × rector_discount × calibration. Baseline comes from the upgrade path, the multipliers compound, the Rector discount lands after them, and the team calibration factor is applied last.
failing: hours = number of extensions × 8. Multipliers and Rector coverage are too project-specific to model.
Take the baseline and add the multipliers and the Rector discount as percentages on top.
